Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the New Zealand's reply. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Devon Conway and Tom Latham are the two openers for New Zealand. Asitha Fernando has the ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Overall, the hosts have dominated and posed a hefty total of 602 runs. Except Nissanka, all of their batters excelled. The 6th wicket partnership from the K MENDIS' duo was of 200 runs! Dhananjaya de Silva and Dimuth Karunaratne fell a few shy of their half-century. Kamindu Mendis was the standout without a doubt as he scored an unbeaten 182. For the Kiwis, Glenn Phillips picked three wickets while Tim Southee chipped in with one. As we look ahead, the Sri Lankan bowlers will be eager to make an early impact, while the Kiwi openers will look to end this day with no loss. Stay tuned for the New Zealand's reply in a short while...

In the second session, Sri Lanka continued their dominance with Kusal Mendis and Kamindu Mendis forming a solid partnership. Kamindu reached his fifth Test century with a steady innings in the 90s, while Kusal played a more aggressive role, scoring a brisk fifty. The pair added an impressive 117 runs off 30.3 overs, punishing loose deliveries from the New Zealand bowlers. The Kiwi bowlers failed to pick any wickets in the second session. Later, the Lankans declared for a 602 in the third session without losing a wicket.

SRI LANKA HAS DOMINATED THE FIRST INNINGS! They are in a strong position, having scored 602 runs! New Zealand started the day under pressure and struggled with the new ball, quickly turning to spin. Glenn Phillips managed to take two crucial wickets in the first session, including that of Angelo Mathews and then another late in the session, keeping New Zealand in the contest.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back!
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

Right then, Sri Lanka have already crossed 400 runs and with still a lot of batting to come and a well-set Kamindu Mendis at the crease, they will look to surpass 500 runs in the next second and maybe declare late in the day as well. New Zealand know that they need to be patient as there is enough in it for the spinners and if they hold on to their chances, wickets will come. Join us at 7.07 am GMT for the post-Lunch session on Day 2.

New Zealand began the day on the back foot and the pacers weren't able to make inroads with a fairly new ball either. They soon reverted to spin from both ends and there were a few really good deliveries bowled. It was Glenn Phillips who got some extra purchase off the rough and bagged the wicket of Mathews before Sri Lanka were able to stitch another partnership together. The Kiwis toiled for a bit again before Phillips was brought back on late in the session and got a crucial breakthrough but the visitors still have a lot of work to do.

New Zealand might have been able to pick up a couple of wickets but in general, Sri Lanka have been dominant with the bat and Kamindu Mendis is playing another sensational knock here. Angelo Mathews fell early in the first session and just looked a bit sluggish as well. Dhananjaya de Silva then came in and played his strokes which presented the Kiwis an opportunity but DDS did well enough to muster up crucial runs. Mendis on the other hand is nearing a century and will look to keep up the good work after the break.

SESSION SUMMARY - 28.3 overs, 96 runs and 2 wickets. A session that seemed to be heading completely towards Sri Lanka but Glenn Phillips has made sure that his side has something to take back into the break and this wicket will help the Kiwis as their shoulders won't drop as much and they will be a bit pumped up when coming back onto the field.

OUT! TAKEN! It's that man again, Glenn Phillips gets the job done for his side and right on the stroke of Lunch, New Zealand have got the breakthrough. Phillips tosses this one up into the rough around off, Dhananjaya de Silva goes for the big sweep shot but is beaten on the bounce and gets a top edge. The ball lobs right up and goes around the backward short leg region. There are fielders around that area but it is the keeper, Tom Blundell who runs after it and dives in to take the catch. DDS departs for 44 (80) and that will be LUNCH ON DAY 2!

Right then, it is a new day, one that the Kiwis will desperately want to make their own but it is Sri Lanka who hold all the cards at the moment and it's all about how they choose to play them. Stick around as cricketing action on Day 2 isn't far away.

New Zealand on the other hand will be grateful for some rest after a long day in the field and would look for early breakthroughs in the first session. There was some turn and bounce already on Day 1 and the spinners should come into play even more on Day 2.

Sri Lanka piled on over 300 runs in 90 overs on Day 1 and lost just 3 wickets as well. Angelo Mathews will be eyeing up a ton as the Lankans will look to score in excess of 450 runs given the position they are in.

Hello and a warm welcome to one and all. It is now time for Day 2 of the second Test match between Sri Lanka and New Zealand at the Galle International Stadium in Galle. Day 1 belonged to the hosts and the Kiwis will look to fightback early on Day 2.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

All the 3 sessions belonged to the Sri Lankans. They will come out on Day 2 and try to bat for as long as they can. New Zealand though have their task cut out. The bowlers have a fairly new ball at their disposal, but New Zealand will certainly need sharper fielding and discipline with the ball to shift momentum on Day 2. Will they be able to pull their socks up? To find out, do join us on 27th September, Friday at 4.30 am GMT. ADIOS!

In the final session we saw 28 overs being bowled where Sri Lanka managed to score 112 runs and lost just a single wicket. They would've loved to remained unscathed but will be delighted to have a solid grip on this game. New Zealand showed great intent, with Glenn Phillips and Ajaz Patel bowling in tandem. Phillips was economical, but Ajaz Patel struggled to find his rhythm early on. Phillips eventually dismissed Chandimal just before the new ball was due, but the session slowed down a bit until the second new ball, with the scoring rate dipping under 3. Despite creating chances with the second new cherry, New Zealand’s fielding let them down, dropping two key catches. Kamindu Mendis and Angelo Mathews capitalized on the errors and constructed a solid unbeaten stand of 85 runs, with Mendis reaching his half-century as they closed the day in a strong position.

A superb day for Sri Lanka. They dominated throughout. They have lost just three wickets with a little over 300 runs on the scoreboard. Surely, a day to forget for the Kiwis. First, they lost the toss, and then were very sloppy in the field as well which did not help their cause.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back, folks! We are back for the final session of the first day of this second Test! The umpires walk out to the middle and a bright sunny sky greets them. The players of New Zealand too take their respective field positions after a brief huddle talk. And Dinesh Chandimal, unbeaten on 106 along with Angelo Mathews on 35, to resume their innings. And it will be Glenn Phillips (7-1-15-0) to get the proceedings underway with the ball after Tea. Here we go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Right then, New Zealand seem to have tightened things up from one end given the way Mitchell Santner has bowled but they need Ajaz Patel to be more attacking as the ball has now started to grip. Sri Lanka will be wanting more of the same and would like Chandimal to convert his ton into the big one from here. Do join us at 9.52 am GMT to find out how the final session on Day 1 pans out.

Angelo Mathews joined Chandimal at the crease and escaped a strangle down the leg side as William O'Rourke overstepped and things just kept on getting worse for the Kiwis. Since the missed opportunity, the Lankan batters have remained largely unbothered with just a few deliveries troubling them.

When play resumed after the Lunch break, Sri Lanka were in a solid position with the bat and they started in control as well. Both Dinesh Chandimal and Dimuth Karunaratne looked fairly settled but suddenly, it was Karunaratne who was run out and their partnership was broken at 124 runs thanks to a good fielding effort from Glenn Phillips.

SESSION SUMMARY - 30 overs, 92 runs and 1 wicket. Another long and engrossing session of Test cricket has gone by but at the Tea break on Day 1, Sri Lanka seem to be firmly in control with the bat. New Zealand were made to toil hard in the field and they only have a run out to show for it in the second session.
Negotiated well by Chandimal. Tossed up on the stumps, Dinesh Chandimal defends it on the front foot. And that will be TEA ON DAY 1.

Right then, New Zealand have it all to do in the post-Lunch session but with what we have seen so far, the spinners will certainly be in play. The pitch is quite dry and there is some rough as well and the Kiwis might look to use Glenn Phillips as the one to attack. Sri Lanka will want more of the same though. Join us at 7.32 am GMT for the second session on Day 1.

New Zealand were soon handed another opportunity to get rid of Karunaratne, this time Ajaz Patel beating him in flight and creating a stumping opportunity but keeper Tom Blundell fumbled it big time. In the next hour or so, Dinesh Chandimal and Dimuth Karunaratne played to their strengths and barely gave any more opportunities. Karunaratne still looked a bit shaky but Chandimal racked up the runs and brought up his 30th Test fifty. The duo then piled on 100 runs exactly for the second wicket before the players went off for Lunch.

New Zealand had to field first which was not ideal in these conditions but skipper Tim Southee gave them the perfect start with the wicket of Pathum Nissanka. Southee and William O'Rourke were then able to pile on the pressure as the latter created a catching opportunity in the slips which was put down by Daryl Mitchell. Dimuth Karunaratne then used this life to muster up some runs as well.

102 runs in 32 overs and just one wicket down - a session that belonged well and truly to Sri Lanka and they will be very pleased with it. New Zealand bowled well in patches but it really was the fielding that let them down on a couple of big occasions. An extended session this first one due to some rain early on but it certainly was engrossing.

Commentary.Commentary: Interesting discussion between Russell Arnold and Mitchell McClenaghan on air. Normally, with the new ball, one sees fast bowlers keep the seam upright, to aid conventional swing. But Tim Southee and Will O'Rourke are holding the seam a bit differently. It is not cross-seam either. Arnold decides to delve deeper into this and asks, thankfully to the benefit of all listening, as to why this is the case. McClenaghan then reminds everyone that in the inaugural World Test Championship final, Southee had dismissed Rohit Sharma, with a different type of delivery - called the THREE-QUARTER SEAM. This name has been christened by the Kiwis themselves, as they are the creators of the same. In this position, the ball is not exactly held cross seam which is why, it is being called as three-quarter seam and then the bowler can either get it to straighten or jag it back in. The variation delivery can be bowled especially to left-handed batters. The concentration has to be on the fact that there should not be any breaking of the wrist. If there is any breaking of the wrist, the seam kind of wobbles too much. That wrist has to be right behind the ball. Wow. We just keep learning every day, don't we? Thank you, Mitch!

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the 2nd Test to get underway! The umpires are out in the middle and the visuals from earlier show Nishan Peiris getting his maiden Test cap. The Kiwi players are seen in a huddle before taking their places on the field. It will be the pair of Dimuth Karunaratne and Pathum Nissanka to open the innings for Sri Lanka. Skipper, Tim Southee will take the new ball for New Zealand. Let's play...

Tim Southee, the captain of New Zealand says that you want to bat first in this part of the world but they gave themselves a chance in the previous game. Informs that they are going in with the same team and is counting on them to get the job done. Adds that last time around it was a first Test after a while and just want to tweak a few things overall.

Dhananjaya de Silva, the skipper of Sri Lanka says that they will bat first as the pitch looks firm with less grass and it looks pretty flat as well. Adds that they would like a few more runs than the last game and adds that Nishan Peiris has done well in the domestic circuit.

PITCH REPORT - Farvez Maharoof is pitchside. He starts by saying that they have moved to pitch 7 from pitch 5 and this one looks a lot drier and the spinners will come into play soon. Reckons that any score of 350 and above in the first innings should be a good one.

Right then, the first Test went into the final day and thankfully, there wasn't that much of rain around. There is the threat of rain throughout the next five days as well but let's hope that we get to see few interruptions and more cricketing action. Stick around as the toss and team sheets aren't far away.

New Zealand haven't had a great time so far in the subcontinent and with a crucial series against the mighty Indians on the horizon, the Kiwis will be desperate to take vital WTC points from Sri Lanka in order to keep their chances of another final alive. They did show glimpses of their best in that first Test match but the batting in that fourth innings was a letdown with only Rachin Ravindra adapting brilliantly to the spin-friendly conditions late in the game. Tim Southee will be hoping that his batters step up and also his bowlers are able to control things a bit better this time around.

Sri Lanka have a spotless record against the Kiwis at Galle and that win in the first Test has now propelled them to third in the WTC points table, leaving them with an outside chance of making it to the final. It was really a gritty showing as the Lankans managed to channel their best from the win against England at the Oval against New Zealand. Prabath Jayasuriya and Ramesh Mendis did a fine job with the ball whereas Kamindu Mendis was the lone centurion of the first game. The Lankans will now look to clean sweep the series.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 1 of the 2nd Test match between Sri Lanka and New Zealand at the Galle International Stadium in Galle. The hosts lead the series 1-0 and if the first game was anything to go by, we might be in for some riveting action over the course of the next five days or so.
